penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A structured program, done-with-you service, or template library for non-technical builders requires ongoing human curation, coaching, and updates — it cannot be fully automated.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Onboarding non-technical professionals through AI-assisted development workflows typically requires live demos, office hours, or synchronous Q&A to be effective.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Non-technical learners generate high support load as they hit blockers; human-judgement support is the norm in this segment.

rationale: The buyer here is vague — 'non-technical startup employees' spans too wide a range, and there is no named business role with a budget line for 'AI coding guidance.' The single HN post shows a success story but not a validated buyer willing to pay for a course or program; the $4K was earned by the poster doing client work, not by selling a structured service to others. Critically, any viable product in this space (course, coaching, template library) requires ongoing human curation and synchronous support, pushing operational autonomy to 3 — well below the build gate floor of 7.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for a solo non-technical operator running an autonomous Claude factory. A 'done-with-you AI coding program' for startup PMMs would require Youval to personally run onboarding calls, maintain a curriculum, and field support questions — none of which Claude can handle end-to-end. The market signal (one HN post) is also too thin. Drop this and revisit only if a narrower, fully-automatable product angle (e.g. a specific template sold once via Gumroad, no support) emerges.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy build gate (scored 3, floor is 7). Fails buyer_clarity build gate (scored 5, floor is 6). Total 1.7 is well below validate threshold.
